AI 기사요약 메타의 AI 에이전트 '뮤즈' 출시로 구매와 결제를 연결하는 커머스 플랫폼 및 AI 인프라 기업들이 수혜주로 떠오르는 반면, 가격 비교와 서비스 전환이 용이해짐에 따라 금융·보험·여행 등 소비자 관성에 의존해 온 기업들은 실적 타격 우려로 희비가 엇갈리고 있다. 쇼피파이, 뮤즈와 협업에 주가 급등 상품 데이터·배송망 갖춘 월마트 주목 SNS 인기 높은 브랜드도 수혜 기대 고객 이탈 우려에 보험·통신·여행 약세 메타의 개인 인공지능(AI) 에이전트 '뮤즈'가 상품 검색과 예약, 결제까지 처리하자 관련 기업의 희비가 엇갈리고 있다. 상품 추천을 실제 구매로 연결할 수 있는 커머스 플랫폼과 AI 인프라 업체는 수혜주로 꼽힌다. 반면 AI가 소비자의 가격 비교와 서비스 변경을 대신하면 금융·보험·여행업체의 수익 구조가 흔들릴 것이라는 우려가 나온다. 뮤즈는 이용자의 지시에 따라 상품을 검색·비교하고 여행을 예약하거나 메시지를 보내는 AI 에이전트다. 지난 8일 출시된 후 챗GPT를 제치고 미국 애플 앱스토어 무료 앱 부문 1위에 올랐다. 월마트 · 쇼피파이 수혜 기대 한경 프리미엄9의 모든 콘텐츠는 한국경제신문의 저작물로 저작권법의 보호를 받습니다. 사전 허가 없는 무단 전재·복제·배포·캡처 공유·AI 학습 활용 및 상업적 이용을 금합니다. 위반 시 서비스 이용 제한 및 민형사상 법적 책임이 발생할 수 있습니다. 무료 열람 혜택으로 기사를 읽으셨습니다. 한경 프리미엄9을 구독하고 무제한으로 만나보세요. 구독하기 AI 뉴스 Q&A 더 궁금한 점이 있으신가요? 읽으면서 머릿속에 맴돌던 질문들, 앨리스가 대답해 드릴게요. 인공지능(AI)을 활용해 생성되었으며, 일부 내용에 오류가 있을 수 있습니다. AI 포인트 뷰 이전 분석 종목 다음 분석 종목 본 서비스의 AI가 제공하는 종목 정보는 정보 제공 목적의 참고 자료일 뿐, 투자 권유·자문·추천에 해당하지 않습니다. 투자에 따른 손실 책임은 사용자에게 있습니다. 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 양지윤 돈이 되는 뉴스를 전하겠습니다. 오세성 기자 한국경제신문 국제부 오세성 기자입니다. 국내 산업·부동산 현장을 거치고 현재는 국제부에서 해외 경제·산업 이슈를 취재합니다. 2020년 한국경제 디지털 대상 최우수 기자코너상, 2022년 한국경제 디지털 대상 우수 기자상, 2024년 한경닷컴 우수 기자상 등을 수상했습니다. sesung@hankyung.com 기사댓글 개의 댓글이 있습니다. 댓글 닫기

Waymo’s latest expansion strategy: teenagers
items.d: Waymo is opening its robotaxi service to teenagers aged 13 to 17 in Nashville, its second city to offer rides to minors.
items.fullText: Waymo will allow teenagers as young as 13 to use its robotaxi service in Nashville as the Alphabet-owned company looks to scale its business by reaching a new group of riders. Nashville is the second city to offer Waymo teen accounts; the company kicked off its teen account program in Phoenix last year. And more cities are likely to follow, according to the company. A Waymo spokesperson told TechCrunch that its expansion to Nashville will be the “first of many” teen launches across multiple markets that use the Waymo app in the coming months. The spokesperson said it will offer teen accounts in cities where its operations are mature and local regulations allow it. Nashville is a relatively new market for Waymo, although it has support from local leaders to offer the service to teens. The company launched its service in a 50-square-mile area of Nashville in April 2026, and earlier this month, its robotaxis became available on the Lyft app. Waymo’s ridership has skyrocketed over the past two years — a trajectory largely driven by the rapid succession of new markets. Paid robotaxi trips grew tenfold from 50,000 per week in May 2024 to more than half-a-million per week earlier this year. Over that same time span, Waymo has launched robotaxi services in a dozen cities. In the past month alone, the company opened robotaxi services in Denver, Las Vegas, San Diego, and Tampa. The company’s introduction of teen accounts provides another means of growth — this one targeted at a demographic that relies on parents or public transit to get to school, work, or activities. There are few limits to the service. The teen account must be connected to a parent or guardian, but once activated, teens can hail autonomous rides anywhere in Waymo’s service area in Nashville — and bring their friends along. Waymo told TechCrunch that teen account holders can bring up to three guests ages 13 to 17. The company didn’t share how these ages would be verified.

items.fullText: Why Deploying Physical AI at Scale Demands Safety at Every Layer As autonomous vehicles, robots and other AI-driven machines take on more complex tasks in the physical world, safety must extend across every layer of the system. September 21, 2026 by Riccardo Mariani 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead. Physical AI is moving rapidly from research to large-scale deployment. By 2035, ABI Research projects an installed base of 49 million level 3-5 autonomous vehicles (AVs) , while Omdia estimates that roughly 60 million industrial robots will be deployed between 2026 and 2035 . As these machines enter roads, factories, warehouses and other environments shared with people, safety must scale with them. Physical AI safety means proving that AI-driven machines — AVs , humanoid robots , industrial robots and more — behave safely when their decisions turn into physical action. That requires safety across the hardware, software, AI, operating environment and deployment lifecycle — not a one-time check before deployment. Why Is Safety the Key to Scaling Physical AI? After years of testing and benchmarking, AVs continue to expand commercially. That progress has required developers to demonstrate how automated systems address potential hardware and software failures, limitations in intended functionality and AI-specific risks. Robotics is approaching a similar inflection point as autonomous machines move into factories, warehouses and other environments shared with people. Across physical AI, manufacturers, regulators, insurers and workplace safety teams need evidence that hardware, software, AI behavior and operating environments can work together safely without human intervention. items.fullText: Physical AI Takes the Wheel: How the World’s Robotaxi Leaders Are Building With NVIDIA Technologies NVIDIA’s modular, full-stack robotaxi pipeline — a three-computer solution spanning AI training, simulation and in-vehicle computing — is being adopted across the robotaxi ecosystem. September 10, 2026 by Ali Kani 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! The global robotaxi market — physical AI’s first commercial breakthrough — is projected to reach $400 billion by 2035 , with over 6 million commercial vehicles in operation as driverless fleets are already moving people through some of the world’s busiest and most complex streets. Deploying a driverless vehicle is one challenge. Scaling a fleet is a next-level computing challenge; it means delivering the same safe, reliable performance across thousands of vehicles. Meeting those demands requires enormous amounts of compute across the robotaxi development lifecycle, from preparing and training AI models to simulating and validating driving behavior, as well as real-time processing in the vehicle. NVIDIA provides an open platform for AI training , simulation and safety validation , with libraries, software development kits, workflows and models that developers can use alongside their own technology stacks. Every major robotaxi program operating at commercial scale today is running on NVIDIA’s modular stack, spanning AI training, simulation, in-vehicle computing — or a combination of the three — to develop and deploy fleets at scale. What Is a Robotaxi Technology Stack? A robotaxi technology stack is the end-to-end set of technologies used to develop, validate and deploy autonomous vehicles (AVs) — from data and AI model training to simulation, safety validation and real-time in-vehicle computing. NVIDIA’s robotaxi and AV platform brings these capabilities together in a three-computer solution: the model training computer, simulation and validation computer, and in-vehicle computer.
